title: Insurance Programme
summary: Every insurance question used to be a request to a colleague. Fifteen years of records sat in three places that only pointed at each other by number. I linked them once, then answered the recurring questions with dashboards and everything else with an assistant.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: PRD, data model, dashboards, AI assistant, auto report, phone layout

facts.label: Stack
facts.value: Feishu Bitable / Spark / Aily · React · NestJS · LLM API

sections.heading: The problem
paragraphs: A manager asks — this year's motor loss ratio, how many claims are still open. Someone opens the share drive, finds the right files, counts by hand and writes a short reply. Hours, sometimes days. The records were never wrong; they were an insurance summary, a claims list and a folder of policy PDFs that referred to each other only by number.

sections.heading: Link once, answer two ways
paragraphs: Open a class and its policies come with it, each with its PDF attached; switch to claims and filter by policy year or status — without opening another file.
The questions asked every month became dashboards: premium by class, broker share, trend, loss ratio. Anything beyond them goes to the assistant.
bullets: Scope — it answers only from our tables and the policy documents inside them
Law — legal points cite the references we specified, for a specialist to confirm
Tools — it reads the policy PDFs and draws its own charts

sections.heading: From dashboard to report
paragraphs: When a view has to be shared, pick a year, a range and the sections: the figures come from the database and the narrative is drafted by a language model, out as a four-page Word file ready to edit. The same system is re-laid out for the phone — key fields first, details on tap.

sections.heading: What the public demo withholds
paragraphs: The employer is not named. Aggregates are synthetic and badged as such; record-level fields render as explicit "Redacted" bars; the assistant is a visual replica that says so instead of inventing answers.
